clue.text: Play in main area behind bars?

indicators.note: behind places the area letter after the bars, at the back

parts.note: main means chief or principal, which is major
two bars, BAR and BAR

explanation.surface: A drama staged in a big prison yard, with the whole set behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: MAJOR BARBARA is a play by George Bernard Shaw; the surface pretends the play is set in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's comedy about a Salvation Army officer is a stage work, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Police arresting ill, sad criminal — did he take the silver?

definitions.note: a definition by example: a silver winner is a medallist; phrased as a question about a person

indicators.note: arresting means holding in, so the police word goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of ill and sad are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police detain a sickly, miserable crook and wonder whether he stole the silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the silver' reads like theft, fitting the criminal surface, but it means winning second place.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver winner at the Olympics or similar competitions is awarded a medal, making that athlete a medal winner.

clue.text: English girls or French boys wear these

definitions.meaning: Jean is a girl's name in English and a boy's name in French; the plural names them
second sense: denim trousers people wear

explanation.walkthrough: Jean is a woman's name in Britain but a man's name in France, so the plural covers both groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim trousers are a garment worn daily by many, so the plural name doubles as clothing.

clue.text: Frilly neckwear fashionable worn by a bruiser

parts.note: a ruff is a pleated Elizabethan collar

indicators.note: worn by means carried inside, so the a goes within the fashion word

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A tough guy turns out wearing a trendy frilled Elizabethan collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruiser is a big, aggressive brawler, and a ruffian is a violent thug: synonyms.

clue.text: Way of playing along with foolish nation

parts.note: along with means and, in addition

indicators.note: foolish suggests something silly or disordered, so the letters of nation are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manner of performance adopted by a silly country.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDANTINO is a tempo marking in music, a little faster (or slower, by some) than andante.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo direction, telling a performer how to play a passage.

clue.text: Polish up hide of neat? Maybe overzealous tanner did

definitions.note: past tense: someone who sunbathes too keenly burnt

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to polish is to rub

indicators.note: the hide is the outer skin, so the first and last letters of neat are taken

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a leather tanner working on cattle hide (neat means cattle).
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle, so 'hide of neat' looks like cowhide; the tanner is actually a sunbather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbather who overdoes it gets sunburn, so the past tense describes what that person's skin did.

clue.text: Salvage edging around lace pants

indicators.note: around puts the rim word on both sides of the shuffled letters

parts.note: a rim is an edge

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so lace is rearranged

explanation.surface: Rescuing lace-trimmed underwear, pants being British for knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to recover or rescue it, which is to reclaim it.

clue.text: Very comfortable partners with extremely lyrical song and dance

parts.note: W and E, West and East, are partners at bridge

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, the ends of lyrical

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, a to-do

explanation.surface: Couples performing a very poetic musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, West and East play as partners, giving WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-off means being comfortable in money terms, so very comfortable is wealthy.

clue.text: Fight half of Leonidas's forces?

indicators.note: half of means only the first four of the eight letters are used

parts.note: Leonidas was king of Sparta, leading the Spartans at Thermopylae

explanation.surface: A question about splitting the army of the Spartan king Leonidas.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or argue, a form of fighting.

clue.text: Happy, say, having ended war finally? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, a run within them

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is cheerful now the war is over at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' looks like an adjective; with a capital it is one of Snow White's seven companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of the seven small companions in Snow White, an example indicated by 'say'.

clue.text: Certainly not dear daughter with patchier vagrant

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters of patchier are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter who is far from beloved, living with a scruffier tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a term of affection; it means expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means expensive, so something not at all expensive is extremely cheap.

clue.text: Gay bachelor abducted by aliens, surprisingly

indicators.note: abducted by means carried off inside, so the bachelor letter goes within the others
surprisingly signals that aliens appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a single man snatched by extraterrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: Gay as an adjective describes same-sex attraction, and a woman attracted to women is lesbian.

clue.text: Most of literary works getting advance publicity

indicators.note: works means works over or rearranges, so the remaining letters are shuffled
most of means the last letter of literary is dropped

explanation.surface: Most book releases come with a promotional campaign beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun for books; it is a verb telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer is a preview shown before release, a form of promotion ahead of time.

clue.text: Dramatist, current Scottish eminence, entertaining society

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, as a host holds guests

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, an eminence being high ground

explanation.surface: A playwright and a Scottish dignitary of today hosting a social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eminence' suggests a VIP; here it is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian author of A Doll's House, a playwright.

clue.text: Rebuff and rejections for reporter's short feature

parts.note: to rebuff is to snub

indicators.note: for the reporter means as spoken aloud, so the word heard is respelt

parts.note: noes are refusals

explanation.surface: A journalist's brief article about being snubbed and turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short feature' looks like a brief news article; it is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose is short and turned up, so it is a stubby facial feature.

clue.text: Inconvenience of ministerial department cutting wages?

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the department sits inside the wages word

parts.note: wages are income
MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: Complaining about the trouble caused by a government department slashing pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting wages' reads as a pay cut; here MOD cuts into INCOME.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode is a formal verb meaning to trouble or put someone out.

clue.text: Military unit ditching gallons, controlling waste discharge

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away, so the gallons letter is removed

parts.note: a contingent is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers dumping fuel cans while managing sewage outflow.
explanation.definitionFit: Being continent means having control over the bladder and bowels.

clue.text: Impression made by earl, with crazy hugging no good

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the no-good letters go inside

parts.note: raving means mad

explanation.surface: An aristocrat makes a poor show embracing someone wild and useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' sounds like the effect someone makes; it is a printed image from an engraved plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print taken from an incised plate, an impression made on paper.

clue.text: Landing in urban area in Holland, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: Dutch means from Holland
a town is an urban area

explanation.surface: An aircraft touching down in a Dutch city.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of DUTCH TOWN to get the sound of TOUCH DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchdown is an aircraft's arrival on the ground at the end of a flight.

clue.text: Resin from wood, somewhat hard on top

indicators.note: on top puts the hard letter above, first in this down entry

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
ash is a tree and its timber
-ish means somewhat

explanation.surface: Tree sap from timber that is fairly firm on its surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is cannabis resin, the compressed sticky product of the hemp plant.

clue.text: Spin about government — it has a point

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin
on means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Political spin about the government, which has a point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it has a point' reads as conceding an argument; it is literal sharpness.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a sharp tine on a fork, something with a sharp tip.

clue.text: Gathered in mansion before party

indicators.note: before puts the mansion word ahead of the party

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: Guests assembled at a stately home ahead of a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Things piled up have been accumulated or heaped together.

clue.text: First of messages I'd sent off in Outlook

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of messages
off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of I'd sent are rearranged

explanation.surface: Emails I'd sent sitting in Microsoft Outlook, the first message going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlook' looks like the email program; it is an attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a fixed attitude or point of view, a person's way of seeing things.

clue.text: Philosopher's works

definitions.meaning: The 's stands for is, joining the two senses

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possession but works as 'is', linking the philosopher to the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: J.S. Mill wrote On Liberty, and a mill is an industrial plant or factory.

clue.text: Ex-president wants man I'm not sure is more loyal

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so the man is taken away

parts.note: Harry Truman was a former US president
taken as written
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: A former US leader needs a reliable aide, hesitating about who is most faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Truer is the comparative of true in its sense of faithful, so it means more faithful.

clue.text: I'm going to breezy westward Adriatic region

parts.note: I'll means I will, I'm going to

indicators.note: westward in an across entry means read from right to left

parts.note: airy means breezy

explanation.surface: Someone announcing a trip to a windy western Balkan coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: Illyria is the ancient region on the east Adriatic coast, and the setting of Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyria was an ancient land along the eastern shore of the Adriatic Sea.

clue.text: Teacher in nightspot turned up AC/DC

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a bar is a nightspot
slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

explanation.surface: A teacher showed up at a club where the rock band AC/DC was playing.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC is also a rock band, but here it is slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious teacher; the word means my master.

clue.text: Being too weary, oddly, to undo dog's clothing

indicators.note: clothing means dressing around, so the dog's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Lassie is the famous film collie; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of to undo are taken

explanation.surface: Struggling, exhausted, to unfasten a pet's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is a state of physical or mental tiredness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Give a name to capital, one in the Middle East

definitions.note: a place in the Middle East: the definition names where the city is

parts.note: to dub is to name
capital as an exclamation means excellent, top grade, which is A
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Naming a capital city in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a place in the Middle East, the city in the United Arab Emirates.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is a city and emirate of the United Arab Emirates, on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Cutting around nutty tart selling like hot cakes

indicators.note: around means the cutting word goes on both sides of the shuffled letters

parts.note: chopping means cutting

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so tart is rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker slicing a nut tart, which is flying off the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutty' looks like a description of the tart; it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping record is a best seller, at number one in sales.
